name: Hashrate-commitment momentum confluence — miners re-arm a real trend
rationale: Miners are the most capital-committed, slowest-moving participants in BTC: deploying or re-energizing hashpower is a multi-month capex decision, so a rising network hashrate is a costly signal that the people who must literally burn electricity to secure the chain are betting it stays worth securing. The thesis: when btc_hashrate crosses UP through a fitted floor (miner-commitment regime turns on) AND medium-term price momentum (ret_Nd) is already positive, the miner re-arm CONFIRMS that the trend is backed by structural conviction rather than thin speculative drift — go long spot. We hold while momentum persists and exit when momentum rolls over (ret_Nd cross_down) or miners capitulate (btc_hashrate cross_down). Hashrate is a slow, drifting series so it is read ONLY via cross_up/cross_down (never a raw level). Disconfirmer (core falsifier): the edge must come from hashrate CONFIRMING momentum, not from momentum alone — if removing the btc_hashrate cross_up arm and keeping only the ret_Nd>floor filter yields equal-or-better deflated Sharpe, hashrate is redundant and this is just plain momentum already covered by the vol/funding-gated specs. Low-confidence until OOS; the Gate decides.
catalyst: btc_hashrate crosses up (miner-commitment regime turns on) while medium-term price momentum is positive
